clue.text: Wave hit shore, we fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine or dress up, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A beachgoer imagines the surf breaking on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the theme: the 1923 FA Cup Final is known as the White Horse Final after a police horse that helped clear the crowd from the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A white horse is a wave whose crest breaks into white foam, an idiom used by sailors.

clue.text: Container with dust — objection raised

parts.note: ash is the dust left after burning

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: A dusty container prompts someone to object.
explanation.definitionFit: A washtub is a large vessel for laundry, a kind of container.

clue.text: Public perception of glossy publication? That is about it!

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a mag, short for magazine, is often printed on glossy paper

explanation.surface: A glossy magazine is said to shape how the public sees things.
explanation.definitionFit: A public image is the impression people at large hold of someone, their reputation.

clue.text: Bird's unusual motion, edging at first upwards

indicators.note: in a down clue, upwards means those letters are written from bottom to top
at first asks for the opening letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: the first letters of unusual, motion and edging

explanation.surface: A bird creeps forward with an odd sideways motion.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Somewhat upfront, I'm exclaiming "Start at 1A 11A not like this"

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of upfront, all of I'm and the start of exclaiming

explanation.surface: An outspoken person announces that the kick-off was late.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1923 final kicked off about three quarters of an hour late because spectators packed onto the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The match did not begin punctually: crowds spilling onto the field delayed the kick-off.

clue.text: Society favourite upset, far from happy, quit

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
down means low in spirits, far from happy

explanation.surface: A society darling, upset and miserable, walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down is to resign from a post, which is to quit it.

clue.text: Bring back bags of money in end

indicators.note: bring back tells us to take the word in reverse order

parts.note: pots of money means a great deal of it

explanation.surface: Someone wants the money returned in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something is to bring it to an end, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Effect of sun seen oddly in train

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in the odd positions: first, third and fifth

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of train

explanation.surface: Passengers on a train notice the sunshine's effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A tan is the browning of skin caused by exposure to sunlight.

clue.text: Frenzy after friend ignores New Zealand horse

indicators.note: after places the friend's word before the remains of frenzy

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: ignores means the letters for New Zealand are left out of the word frenzy

explanation.surface: A friend gets into a frenzy over a horse, and New Zealand is somehow involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A palfrey is an old word for a gentle riding horse, especially one for a lady.

clue.text: A service going up at distance

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A military service aircraft rises far off.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an adverb meaning far away, at a distance.

clue.text: Rule safeguarding sci-fi film award perhaps

indicators.note: safeguarding means the rule holds the film inside it

parts.note: a statute is a written law, a rule
E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 science-fiction film

explanation.surface: A regulation protects a science-fiction film's chance of a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A statuette is a small figurine, the form many awards such as the Oscar take.

clue.text: Ruling out further discussion, finances cut by 50%, ultimately cruel

indicators.note: cut by half means only the first four of the word's eight letters are kept
ultimately points to the last letter of cruel

parts.note: the closing letter of cruel

explanation.surface: A harsh budget halving is announced as the end of the argument.
explanation.walkthrough: With 1-across this names the theme, the 1923 FA Cup Final.
explanation.definitionFit: A final decision is conclusive, admitting no further argument or appeal.

clue.text: Hint about Brussels business connection

indicators.note: about means the hint word goes around the other

parts.note: a tip is a hint
Brussels is shorthand for the European Union, whose main institutions are there

explanation.surface: A tip-off about a deal involving Brussels.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-up is a merger or partnership between companies, a business link.

clue.text: Dog and what it might do, check!

parts.note: a dog may poo, a childish word for defecate
ch is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A dog owner warns to watch out for what the animal leaves behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooch is an informal word for a dog.

clue.text: Chatroom guy maybe not fully up-to-date with schedule on return

indicators.note: not fully means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: modern means up to date

indicators.note: on return means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: A chatroom user is not quite current with the timetable on his way back.
explanation.definitionFit: A moderator oversees an online forum, keeping posts in order; he is one example of a chatroom figure.

clue.text: Thanks teacher leaving capital getting pile of cards

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks

indicators.note: leaving means the teacher's word goes out of the capital's name

parts.note: London is the UK's capital
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher leaves the capital after thanks, taking a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the talon is the stock: the pile of undealt cards left on the table.

clue.text: Wanderers' home — blessing to have military person involved

indicators.note: involved means the officer is wrapped up inside the blessing

parts.note: a boon is a blessing
Lt is a lieutenant, a military officer

explanation.surface: Travellers are glad to have a soldier staying with them.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolton Wanderers are an English football club, one of the two teams in the 1923 final.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolton is the Lancashire town that is home to the football club Bolton Wanderers.

clue.text: Story about extremely sartorial fabric

indicators.note: about means the story word surrounds those letters

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib

indicators.note: extremely means the outermost letters of sartorial

parts.note: the first and last letters of sartorial

explanation.surface: A tale about a very stylish cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread or the fabric woven from it, used for stockings.

clue.text: Elm, yew, initially both unfamiliar in playing area

indicators.note: unfamiliar means the letters are not in their usual shape, so they are rearranged
initially points to the first letter of both

parts.note: the first letter of both

explanation.surface: Two trees, elm and yew, look strange growing on a pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Wembley is the London stadium where the 1923 final was the first match played.
explanation.definitionFit: Wembley Stadium is England's national football ground, a venue where games are played.

clue.text: Pained expression in sea off Nice that may be cutting

indicators.note: in means the cry of pain is placed inside the French word for sea

parts.note: mer is French for sea, as spoken off the French Riviera city of Nice
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Someone yelps in pain while swimming in the Mediterranean, perhaps cut on a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A mower is a machine for cutting grass, so it is something doing the cutting.

clue.text: Boys painted Medical Officer in strange attire

indicators.note: in means the doctor's letters are set inside the rearranged attire
strange means the letters of attire are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist painted lads with a doctor in odd clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoretti are the chubby winged infant cupids shown in Renaissance art.

clue.text: Players bearing with poor performer

parts.note: west is a compass bearing
a ham is a bad, overacting performer

explanation.surface: Actors tolerate a weak member of the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham United were Bolton's opponents in the 1923 final.
explanation.definitionFit: West Ham United is a London football club, so a team of players.

clue.text: Seek to impress daughter censored in print

parts.note: to woo is to try to win someone over
censored material has been cut

explanation.surface: A suitor's daughter is censored in the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcut is a print made from a carved wooden block.

clue.text: To begin with, that was one night in London for 16 with this result

indicators.note: to begin with asks for the first letter of each of the following words

parts.words: that was one night in London
parts.note: the opening letters of the six words that, was, one, night, in, London

explanation.surface: A memorable night out in London is recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: The 16 in the clue is the entry BOLTON: Bolton Wanderers won the 1923 final two goals to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-nil scoreline is a 2-0 win, the result Bolton achieved in the final.

clue.text: Person easily deceived by recycled article in Palace location

parts.note: a lamb is a meek, innocent person, easily fooled

indicators.note: recycled means made into something new, so the article's letters are reworked into a fresh order

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A gullible person is taken in by a reused item.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambeth Palace, in south London, is the official London residence of the Archbishop of Canterbury.

clue.text: Is much bigger than FDR was — bizarre!

indicators.note: bizarre signals the letters come out strangely ordered

explanation.surface: Someone finds it odd that something towers over a US president.
explanation.walkthrough: FDR is Franklin D. Roosevelt, the US President.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwarf something is to make it look tiny by comparison, so to be far larger.

clue.text: Public dispute about hotel's downfall

indicators.note: about means the public dispute surrounds the hotel letter

parts.note: overt means open, public
a row is a dispute
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An open argument erupts over a hotel's collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: An overthrow is the removal of a ruler or regime from power, their fall.

clue.text: Fuss excessively about dinner's starter

indicators.note: about means that letter sits inside

parts.note: too means excessively, as in too much

indicators.note: starter means the first letter of dinner

parts.note: the first letter of dinner

explanation.surface: Someone frets too much over the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion or fuss.

clue.text: Provide better weapons for military at back, munitions at the outset

parts.note: rear means at the back

indicators.note: at the outset points to the first letter of munitions

parts.note: the first letter of munitions

explanation.surface: An army supply plan for the back lines, with munitions coming first.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to equip forces again with fresh or improved arms.

clue.text: Article used in Milan a non-drinker holds in inclined position

indicators.note: holds means the non-drinker goes around the article

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, someone who takes no alcohol
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: A teetotaller in Milan is caught up with an article.
explanation.definitionFit: Atilt is an adverb meaning tilted, leaning at an angle.

clue.text: Feature of 1A 11A — boast by Duke

parts.note: to crow is to boast

explanation.surface: A duke brags about the famous final.
explanation.walkthrough: A vast crowd, perhaps 200,000, packed into Wembley for the 1923 final.
explanation.definitionFit: The huge throng of spectators who spilled onto the pitch is what the match is remembered for.

clue.text: Day featured in Old English poem

indicators.note: featured in means the day letter appears inside the other piece

explanation.surface: A day is celebrated in a poem written in Old English.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem addressed to a subject.

clue.text: Something at 18 goes with hat

parts.note: a turn is a go, so goes are turns
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Something at the stadium is worn with a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is WEMBLEY; the turnstiles were overwhelmed by the crowd in 1923.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnstile is a revolving entry gate found at stadiums like Wembley.

clue.text: Reportedly a remarkable amount of money

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is heard rather than seen, so its sound is taken

parts.note: some can mean remarkable, as in that was some goal

explanation.surface: Word has it that a fortune changed hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is a quantity of money, as in a large sum.

clue.text: Set about crossing European river

indicators.note: crossing means the reversed word spans the European letter
about here means turned round, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to cross a river on the continent.

clue.text: Earliest source of flame? 1A 11A was this at 18

second meaning: the 1923 final was the first game ever played at Wembley
